body:
JohnHendricks <hendri19@indy.net> wrote:

>All things in nature have built in obsolence, particullarly those things 
>made by man... wether planned or not is of no consequence. The question 
>is; "What's it good for," and "do I get my money's worth before it craps 
>out," or "how much can I unload it for on the next guy," before it 
>totally falls apart. Technology is neither good or bad, it simply is a 
>consequence of human nature and therefore an integral part of nature.

>Advancement of technology provides a sideline benefit to mankind, in that 
>it evolves the state of the art and continues to produce work, therefore 
>is a stabilizing benefit to the society of man. 

some would argue that technology is what destabilizes society, 
they would say that you can't make rapid, drastic changes in the
technology and the economy of a society without causing rapid changes
in all other aspects of the society as well, and that such rapid
changes inevitably break down traditional values.
